claim: emergencyWithdraw(0) returns staked VVS without burning BENCH, letting the exiter keep unbacked BENCH.
evidence: Craftsman.sol:304-312 emergencyWithdraw has no pid!=0 guard and no bench.burn call, unlike leaveStaking at 284-302 which burns. enterStaking at 263-282 mints BENCH 1:1.
runtimeTrigger: enterStaking(100 ether), then emergencyWithdraw(0): VVS returned, BENCH balance stays 100 ether, userInfo amount 0.

claim: deposit/withdraw pay pending rewards before the LP transferFrom and before updating user state, so an LP token with a transfer hook can re-enter and double-claim pending rewards.
evidence: Craftsman.sol:220-240 deposit pays pending (lines 226-231) before safeTransferFrom (234) and before user.amount/rewardDebt updates (235-238). Same shape in withdraw 242-261. No reentrancy guard.
runtimeTrigger: Pool LP token whose transferFrom calls back into the sender; deposit(pid, amt) with accrued pending re-enters deposit(pid, 0) and is paid twice.

claim: Pair permit() accepts malleable ECDSA signatures (no low-s / v check in deployed bytecode).
crossReferences: SlowMist N5 (permit malleability, reported Fixed in pre-deployment code)
evidence: Deployed pair 0xbf62c67e... runtime bytecode contains neither the secp256k1 half-order constant nor the curve-order constant; permit revert string is canonical 'VVS: INVALID_SIGNATURE'.
runtimeTrigger: Observer flips (v,s) of a victim permit signature and submits the malleated permit first; same approval lands, victim tx reverts on consumed nonce.

claim: Pair DOMAIN_SEPARATOR is fixed at deployment and never recomputed, enabling cross-chain permit replay after a chain split.
evidence: DOMAIN_SEPARATOR recomputed exactly from name 'VVS Finance LPs', version '1', chainId 25, verifyingContract=pair; canonical UniswapV2ERC20 constructor-time computation.
runtimeTrigger: Cronos chain split preserving chainId 25 and pair addresses; a permit signature valid on one fork replays on the other.

evidence: Craftsman.sol:104 updateMultiplier onlyOwner; 156 setMigrator onlyOwner + 161 migrate public; 114 add / 130 set onlyOwner; 324 distributeSupply onlyOwner. Owner 0x7ed52E... is an EOA (no code).
runtimeTrigger: Owner sets BONUS_MULTIPLIER huge, or sets a malicious migrator and anyone calls migrate(pid).

claim: deposit credits the nominal amount while a fee-on-transfer LP token delivers less, diverging user.amount from actual holdings.
evidence: Craftsman.sol:234-235 safeTransferFrom then user.amount.add(_amount) with no balance-delta measurement; lpSupply in updatePool is balance-based (206).
runtimeTrigger: Owner adds a fee-on-transfer token pool; deposits credit more than delivered.

claim: Direct LP donations to Craftsman inflate lpSupply and dilute accVVSPerShare for all stakers.
evidence: Craftsman.sol:206 and 183: lpSupply = pool.lpToken.balanceOf(address(this)); donations increase the denominator without any user.amount.
runtimeTrigger: Anyone transfers LP tokens directly to Craftsman; subsequent updatePool distributes the same rewards over a larger supply.

claim: A staker who transfers BENCH away cannot leaveStaking (burn reverts), locking their VVS stake.
evidence: Craftsman.sol:284-302 leaveStaking calls bench.burn(msg.sender, _amount) unconditionally; OZ _burn reverts when the caller lacks BENCH balance.
runtimeTrigger: enterStaking(100 ether); transfer BENCH elsewhere; leaveStaking(100 ether) reverts.

claim: updatePool divides by totalAllocPoint, which the owner can drive to 0, bricking reward updates.
evidence: Craftsman.sol:210 vvsReward = multiplier.mul(vvsPerBlock).mul(pool.allocPoint).div(totalAllocPoint); set() at 130-140 lets the owner zero allocations; updateStakingPool leaves pool 0 unchanged when other points sum to 0.
runtimeTrigger: Owner sets all pool allocations to 0; updatePool reverts with division by zero.

claim: distributeSupply can be called repeatedly in succession after a long delay, halving supply and minting team amounts each time.
evidence: VVSInitMintable.sol:31-49: gate is block.timestamp >= nextDistributionTimestamp, then nextDistributionTimestamp advances by a fixed 365-day window (not to now), so a multi-year gap permits back-to-back calls.
runtimeTrigger: Owner waits 3 years, then calls Craftsman.distributeSupply 3 times in a row.
